name: pam-permit-auth
description: Practice-box misconfiguration: inserts `auth sufficient pam_permit.so` at the top of a PAM stack so authentication succeeds with no password. Vars: PAM_FILE (optional, default /etc/pam.d/common-auth).
script:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

pam_file="${PAM_FILE:-/etc/pam.d/common-auth}"

# Guard on the SPECIFIC "auth sufficient pam_permit.so" line, not just any
# mention of the pam_permit.so module name -- Ubuntu's stock common-auth
# already references pam_permit.so in a separate, benign "prime the stack"
# line ("auth required ... pam_permit.so", a no-op safety net placed after
# pam_deny.so so the chain never returns an unset code), so a bare
# `grep -q pam_permit.so` false-positives on that pre-existing line and
# silently skips planting this finding -- confirmed the hard way (149 round).
if [ -f "$pam_file" ] && ! grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*auth[[:space:]]+sufficient[[:space:]]+pam_permit\.so' "$pam_file"; then
    tmp="$(mktemp)"
    printf 'auth\tsufficient\tpam_permit.so\n' > "$tmp"
    cat "$pam_file" >> "$tmp"
    cat "$tmp" > "$pam_file"
    rm -f "$tmp"
fi
